ops.body:
Closed 2026-07-25. All five findings plus both MISSED items fixed and shipped in 491244e, released as codex 1.8.4.

- 1 (revised, major): classify() is read-only again — the stale-.tmp sweep is gone. Verified independently: the only remaining os.Remove calls in registry.go are atomicWrite's own temps and the prune RemoveAll. Reap relocated to dispatch's lane reset, under the exclusive lock, restricted to a lane-local codex-r-* path.
- 2 (revised, major): relative XDG_CACHE_HOME refuses exit 2 before any MkdirAll, base canonicalized via EvalSymlinks, the prune walk is lstat-based so it never descends a symlinked entry, and RemoveAll is gated on canonical containment under the lane lock.
- 3 (confirmed): registerGraceS names the window --await had been enforcing with an unnamed 60-poll counter; classify applies the same policy, so --watch settles instead of hanging.
- 4 (confirmed): prune takes a non-blocking exclusive lane lock and rechecks state, age, and containment before RemoveAll. Non-blocking deliberately — a blocking acquire would stall --ps behind an entire codex run.
- 5 (confirmed): --await runs rejectOutsideScratch on the resolved lane dir before acquiring or creating any lock.
- MISSED-1: --watch pins the generation under a shared lock. Acquired lazily per poll rather than serially at arm — my review caught that the first shape blocked the whole watch behind any single contended lane, which would have traded one defect for a user-visible hang.
- MISSED-2: readPid rejects non-positive, so a corrupt "0" no longer reads alive forever via kill(0,0).

The regression the grace fix would have introduced (classify deleting a live worker's staged reply once an expired lane read died) never shipped — finding 1's fix landed in the same change, which is why they were clustered.

Three goldens encoded the superseded contract and now assert the new one: the sweep test asserts the .tmp survives --collect, the aged pid-less lane reads died and is still never pruned, and the source-shape test pins the defer anchor.

Separately, the flaky lane-reuse golden tracked in 297a048 turned out to be a real production bug in the same lock protocol — the GC finalizer closing the lane lock's fd mid-run — found and fixed as part of this work.
